dossier.architecture: Two-sided intake, transfer pivot and powerful launcher, with compact spring-deployed chain climber.

subsystems.drivetrain: REV modules with Vortex drive and custom TPU tread; team reports frequent wheel replacement.
subsystems.intake: Front/rear pickup feeds a central path; sensors stop the note and a low-friction plate supports it.
subsystems.transfer: Pivoting transfer preserves vertical compression into the launcher.
subsystems.scoring: Four Vortex-powered wheel groups and adjustable launch pivot; tested contact and compression govern geometry.
subsystems.endgame: Constant-force-spring deployment, powered retrieval and magnetic hook retention; side approach leaves harmony room.
subsystems.controls: AprilTag/odometry localization and shot lookup tables support scoring or passing into the protected amp-side area.

versions: Approximately eleven launcher iterations reported. TPU wheels replaced stock tread; hook magnet addressed inconsistent chain engagement.
dossier.analysis: Their role flexibility depended on deliberate pass landing zones, not merely being able to throw a note far. Wheel performance also carried a substantial consumable/service requirement.
limits: Configuration description is tied to the cited interview; not a claim that every unreported shop revision is known.

context_documents.title: 2024-3005 · Contact geometry and fast wheel service both affect available scoring
context_documents.body:
# 2024-3005: Contact geometry and fast wheel service both affect available scoring

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Front/rear intake paths stage a note on low-friction support and feed a pivoting transfer. The launcher uses four Vortex-driven contact groups after tests with fewer contacts. The interview also discusses rapidly replaceable printed wheel components, reporting swaps in under a minute when a replacement is prepared.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team says earlier arrangements did not provide sufficient contact and that additional roller power/placement emerged through testing. Serviceability was deliberately considered for playoff repair windows.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Motor count is the consequence of a contact requirement, not a standalone design target. Each contact must accelerate without deforming the note into a less repeatable state. Repair speed affects how much performance survives a tournament: a fast but fragile part may be viable only if replacement stock and access are designed at the same time.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare slip, note deformation and release speed across contact arrangements. Time an actual module replacement with match-ready tools and verify the resulting alignment.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/rmW-vyC5Gdo](https://youtu.be/rmW-vyC5Gdo)

binder_audit.interpretation: A missing verified binder is an unresolved retrieval result, not evidence the team never published one. Existing interviews/CAD sources remain usable.

source_reviews.title: RoboChargers Surge reveal
facts: Double-sided under-bumper intake, pivoted launcher, diverter for amp/speaker and single telescoping climber.
source_reviews.limitations: Announcement does not define the diverter sequence or all revisions.

source_reviews.title: Surge public CAD and team Q&A
facts: Four Vortex motors avoid mechanical linkage between launcher corners. The team uses side-to-side speed differences to create spin.
One guard prevents notes reaching the climber and another feature supports launcher counterbalance tubing.
The team reports speed within roughly 1% of setpoint over a stated operating range. This is a speed-control account, separate from shot accuracy.
source_reviews.limitations: CAD release thread gives no instrumented shot distributions. The linked model was not measured.

source_reviews.title: Surge Behind the Bumpers
facts: The older record describes note retention on a low-friction plate, a pivot transfer preserving vertical compression and spring-deployed climb hardware.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Surge brings notes in under the bumpers from either end and routes them into a pivoted launcher. A diverter allows that launch assembly to serve speaker and amp. The team describes choosing a motor at each corner to remove cross-launcher mechanical linkages and to vary speed across the note. This makes the important trade visible. The machine saves mechanical couplings but must deliver four coordinated wheel speeds while the transfer presents a note with repeatable compression.
piece_flow: The two entrances converge on a common path. Older material describes sensing and supporting the note on a low-friction plate.
The inherited pivoting handoff maintains compression while delivering the note to the launcher.
The launcher sets angle and wheel speeds. The team identifies an amp/speaker diverter but the exact fork timing remains unresolved.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The shared central route must stay clear of the telescoping hook. The team identified a dedicated guide that prevents a note catching there. Launcher counterbalance tubing also uses local bracket space. Draw a loaded note and the compliant contact patches through the pivot sweep. Include wires, guard edges and a path to extract a note after the machine stops.

subsystems.name: Capture and diverter
subsystems.construction: Team confirms two under-bumper mouths and an amp/speaker diverter. Older corpus describes a central support and moving handoff.
subsystems.operation: Acquire in either drive direction, retain centrally and present to the appropriate release.
subsystems.team_rationale: The reveal establishes the two destinations. Detailed team reasoning for the transfer pivot is inherited.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A common path only helps if a note arriving from either side reaches a common staged position. Unequal approach speed or off-center entry can change how the diverter contacts the rim.
subsystems.interfaces: Entry, staging, pivot and branch need position and speed overlap.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test both entry directions, deliberate partial pickup and restoration after the wrong branch or jam.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact sensor logic and physical diverter geometry.

subsystems.name: Four-motor launcher
subsystems.construction: Four separate Vortex drives and a pivot with tubing counterbalance support.
subsystems.operation: Match wheel speed to the shot and establish a side-to-side difference where spin is wanted.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team cited easier mechanical layout and independently adjustable speeds.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Within-setpoint speed error does not establish speed during the loaded shot. Measure per-wheel droop and recovery with worn notes, at low battery and during drivetrain demand.
subsystems.interfaces: Compression through the feed transition, four independent speed loops and the pivot's repeatable angle.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Log current and wheel velocity before and after feeding. Check whether any one under-speed corner should block release.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured launch dispersions, flywheel inertia and actual current budgets.

subsystems.name: Chain hook and protection
subsystems.construction: Team announces single telescoping climber and describes an anti-snag feature. Older dossier describes spring deployment.
subsystems.operation: Extend to catch the chain while leaving the note route usable.
subsystems.team_rationale: Guard is explicitly there to stop a note catching on the climber.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The guard should stay effective with the hook partly deployed or after a collision changes the nearby gap.
subsystems.interfaces: Hook, note envelope and launcher counterbalance occupy neighboring volumes.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect the guard after hook or launcher service and test note movement with climb hardware stowed.
subsystems.unknowns: Hook load and geometry, verified harmony maneuver and event states.

revisions: Team reported a launcher swap for upgrades and used run-in swerve modules as known-good spares. Exact event configurations remain open.
transferable_principles: Measure launch readiness under the full electrical and piece load when replacing mechanical synchronization with independent drives. Use guards to protect the piece path from adjacent mechanisms.
disconfirming_conditions: Two-sided collection loses value if switching approaches degrades staging. Four independent drives may be excessive when a mechanically coupled layout meets the shot envelope with lower wiring and power cost.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, launcher geometry, diverter sequence and run logs.
recommended_images: CAD release views of shooter corners and climber guard
